title: Define P99 tail SLOs, synthetic canary guards, and progressive traffic-shard rollback criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement: We've historically validated latency SLOs at aggregate P50/P90 levels for hosted text-gen routes, but tail latency (P99+) is the main cause of customer-visible stalls and error escalations during bursts and tenant-specific hotspots. This ticket defines concrete P99 tail SLOs per API route, specifies the synthetic canary suite and traffic-shard gating rules for progressive rollouts, and enumerates precise rollback criteria and acceptance tests for releases that touch scheduling, batching, or routing logic.

Scope:
- Define per-route P99 latency targets and acceptable variability bands (absolute and relative to baseline).
- Create a minimal synthetic canary harness (load profiles + seed prompts) to validate tail behavior pre-rollout.
- Specify traffic sharding percentages and time windows for staged rollouts with automatic rollback triggers.
- Define required monitoring queries, alert thresholds, and on-call playbook links.
- Document acceptance criteria for engineering changes that modify batching, KV cache or routing heuristics.
Out of scope: model quality metrics, billing changes, dedicated capacity contract terms.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route P99 target defined for: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings (values and units documented)
Synthetic canary harness implemented in CI that runs the smoke-profile and produces P99 and error-rate reports within the PR pipeline
Rollout gating policy established: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with minimum observation windows (configurable) and explicit rollback conditions
Automated alerts fire when burn-rate of P99 violations exceeds 3x baseline for a 5-minute window and trigger a circuit-breaker to shift traffic to fallback model variant
Acceptance tests include: stable P99 within band under synthetic burst profile, no increase in 5xx rate above 0.2% absolute, and no increase in downstream queueing beyond 20% over baseline
Runbook and post-mortem template linked; on-call has step-by-step rollback knobs documented and validated in a dry-run
proposed_thresholds: /v1/generate: P99 <= 900ms (baseline 700ms) — soft band +20% allowable during initial rollout
/v1/chat: P99 <= 1200ms (baseline 950ms) — stricter for streaming first-token guarantees
/v1/embeddings: P99 <= 250ms (baseline 200ms) — lightweight route, tight tail target
Error budget: max sustained P99 violation burn-rate of 1% of requests per hour before an automated throttle or fallback
5xx error spike threshold: absolute increase >0.2% over 15m triggers canary abort
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary in staging with synthetic harness (must pass full smoke profile including tail checks)
Phase 1: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes; monitor P99, 5xx, queue depth, queue latency percentiles
Phase 2: 25% for 1 hour with same monitors; require burn-rate < 1.5x and 5xx delta < 0.1%
Phase 3: 100% gradual ramp over 4 hours if previous phases green; otherwise rollback to previous model/variant
Automatic rollback triggers: P99 burn-rate > 3x baseline for 5 minutes OR 5xx delta > 0.2% for 15 minutes
Manual guardrail: SRE or product sign-off required to resume after automated rollback; post-rollback RCA scheduled within 24 hours
monitoring_queries: Synthetic CI: smoke-run returns artifacts: p50,p90,p95,p99,5xx-count; fail PR if p99 exceeds proposed threshold
notes: We must account for tenant-weighted P99: a few noisy tenants can skew cluster-level p99; plan includes tenant-level monitoring and per-tenant circuit-breaker thresholds.
Synthetic profiles should include: small prompt short-response, long-context generation, streaming-first-token latency, and KV-cache-cold sequences.
Discussed with SRE on 2026-03-05: agreed minimum observation windows and that automated rollback must be reversible without data loss.
Design team to provide UX copy for in-console rollout state (percent, phase, reason for abort) — see linked design ticket PM-121002
